transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t get out from under this feeling that I’ve messed everything up. Like I’ve fallen behind at work, and then the apartment situation has gotten out of hand too, and it feels like both of those are my fault in this really heavy way.

It’s not just “I made a mistake,” it’s more like… I keep thinking I’ve ruined things for everyone around me. Like people are having to deal with the consequences of me not keeping up or not handling things the way I should have. And I know maybe that sounds dramatic, but it feels very real to me. I keep turning it over in my head, thinking I should have done more, I should have caught it earlier, I should have been able to control it.

And honestly, part of me feels like I deserve whatever bad thing happens next because of it. That’s the part that scared me enough to come in, I think.
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these thoughts and feelings been going on for more than a couple of weeks?

Yeah… definitely more than a couple of weeks. It’s been, I guess, about a year and two months now.

It started around when that pipe burst and I had to move into the smaller apartment. I don’t know if that sounds like the kind of thing that should knock someone off course for this long, but it did for me. My routines kind of fell apart after that, and I haven’t really been able to get them back in place. Since then it’s just been this ongoing feeling, like things got out of order and I never caught up again.

So, yeah… not recent. It’s been over a year, pretty much.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure or interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… yes, I have. That’s actually been one of the stranger parts, because I can remember what those things used to feel like, but I can’t really get to that feeling now.

Most days I wake up and there’s this kind of flat, heavy sadness already there, like it’s waiting for me before I even do anything. And the things that used to sort of reset me or make me feel like myself… they don’t really land anymore. I used to put on a record and actually listen to it, like sit with it and enjoy the sound of it. Or I’d cook something, even just something simple, and there’d be some satisfaction in doing it right. I’d tinker with electronics too, little repairs or projects, and I could lose track of time in a good way.

Now I might still try to do those things, but it’s like they don’t reach me. The music is just noise, cooking feels like steps to get through, and even messing with electronics feels pointless or kind of exhausting. It’s not that I decided I don’t like them anymore. It’s more like the part of me that responds to them is… muted or blocked off somehow.
Do you find yourself feeling guilty or responsible for things even when it’s not really your fault, or feeling like you’re a bad person because of what’s happened?

Yes… very much. That’s probably the thing I keep circling back to the most.

I know, logically, maybe there are parts of it that weren’t completely in my control, but it doesn’t feel that way. It feels like I let things get away from me — at work, with the apartment, just all of it — and then other people had to deal with the mess because I couldn’t keep up. I keep thinking, if I had been more organized, or stronger somehow, or paid attention sooner, maybe none of this would have happened the way it did.

And then it turns into this bigger thought, like I haven’t just made mistakes, but that I’ve ruined things for everyone. Like I’m the source of the problem. I keep replaying it and I can’t really convince myself otherwise, even when part of me knows that sounds… extreme.

So yes, I feel guilty. And not just guilty, I guess. More like I deserve whatever bad thing comes next because I failed to handle things the way I should have. That thought has been sitting there pretty heavily.

Have you ever had a period of time when you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, along with other symptoms like changes in sleep, appetite, energy, or difficulty concentrating, lasting for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I mean, yes. That’s pretty much what it’s been like.

Most days, almost as soon as I wake up, there’s this flat, heavy sadness already there. It’s not always dramatic, like I’m crying all day or anything, but it’s there in the background and it kind of colors everything. Like I start the day already feeling weighed down, before anything has even happened.

And it’s been that way enough that it doesn’t feel like just a bad mood passing through. The things that used to help me feel normal or sort of reset me don’t really do that anymore. I’ll put on a record, and I know I used to enjoy just sitting with the music, noticing little parts of it, but now it just sort of… doesn’t reach me. Cooking feels the same way. I can go through the motions, chop things, follow steps, clean up after, but there’s no satisfaction in it. And tinkering with electronics used to absorb me in a good way, but now I’ll look at something I meant to fix and it just feels distant, like I can’t connect to why I cared.

So, yes, it’s been most of the day, most days. It’s not like there aren’t moments where I’m distracted or functioning, but underneath it there’s that heaviness.
Has this feeling of sadness or low mood been present most days for at least two years?

No… not two years. It’s been long, and it feels longer than it probably is, but if I’m being accurate, it’s more like about a year and two months.

It really started after the pipe burst and I had to move into that smaller apartment. That’s when everything kind of came apart — not all at once maybe, but my routines got disrupted, and I never really got them back. Since then the low mood has been there most days, but it hasn’t been two full years. It’s been around fourteen months, something like that.

Have you ever had a period of time when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or unusually irritable — where you didn’t need much sleep, talked more than usual, or felt like your thoughts were racing?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re describing.

I mean, I’ve had times where I was tense or restless, or where my mind wouldn’t settle because I was worried about things, but I wouldn’t call it feeling high or energized. It’s not like I suddenly needed less sleep and felt fine, or became unusually talkative, or felt like I could take on everything. If anything, when I’m not sleeping well, I feel worse and more worn down, not charged up.

I guess I’ve been irritable at times, but it feels more like being overwhelmed or frayed, not like this big shift where I’m more driven or wired than usual. I haven’t noticed a period where people were saying I seemed different in that way, or where I felt unusually confident or unstoppable or anything like that.

So… no, I don’t think I’ve had that kind of episode.
Before this past year and two months, have you ever had a period of time when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks, or longer?

Before that? No, not really. I mean, I’ve had bad stretches like anyone, but nothing I’d describe as lasting two weeks or more where I was down like this or lost interest in everything.

This whole thing really started about a year and two months ago, after the pipe burst and I had to move into the smaller apartment. That was kind of the point where my normal routines fell apart, and I never really got them back. So if I’m thinking about before that, I don’t remember a period that felt like this.
